A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLP Memory research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-modeling, hallucination, classification, reasoning, and ablation results in Section 4 and the appendices, although some baseline results are attributed to prior work.

after.justification: v2 reports original QA, general-NLP, hallucination, efficiency, and sensitivity results, alongside retained experimental analyses in its appendices.

M1.justification: Both versions train an all-MLP memory on hidden representations using precomputed kNN targets with self-retrieval excluded, combine KL and cross-entropy losses, and interpolate memory and language-model probabilities. The rewritten method description does not establish a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: v2 adds Natural Questions, WebQA, TriviaQA, HotpotQA, and HaluEval dialogue and QA evaluations, using Wikipedia-2021 for QA and hallucination experiments. FACTOR and StrategyQA evaluations disappear. TruthfulQA, HaluEval summarization, the nine classification/entailment tasks, and WikiText-103/Web scaling experiments remain.

E2.justification: Within retained tasks, v2 removes kNN-LM from the TruthfulQA and HaluEval-Sum comparisons and excludes RAG from summarization. RAG is added to the efficiency comparison. The nine-task comparison retains the existing CPT, LoRA, RAG, and kNN-LM comparator set.

E3.justification: General-NLP and hallucination evaluations contract from three backbones to Mistral, while the new QA experiments use Llama2 and Mistral with a stated compute-matched training budget. TruthfulQA now reports the average of MC1–MC3, and HaluEval reports accuracy instead of the previous summarization precision and arithmetic/harmonic accuracy measures. Efficiency evaluation changes from GPT2 latency with 100M/500M-token datastores to TTFT/TPS with Wikipedia-2021 and dimension-reduced kNN retrieval.

E4.justification: v1's TruthfulQA/Llama2 interpolation sweep is replaced by a wider HaluEval/Mistral sweep across three tasks. The StrategyQA analysis with and without chain-of-thought is removed, and four distinct RAG-versus-memory case studies are added. Loss-weight, layer-selection, output-distribution, target-model, and neighbor-count analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The statements that results are means over five random seeds in v1 Tables 2, 3, and 8 disappear. v2 supplies no replacement run-count or uncertainty reporting. This establishes reduced statistical disclosure, not that fewer runs were performed; neither version reports confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial QA and HaluEval results and replaces existing score sets. For example, Mistral base/MLP nine-task averages change from 72.53/75.37 in v1 Table 3 to 67.86/73.07 in v2 Table 2; incompletely matched settings prevent interpreting this as a performance decline. New timing results also use different conditions, while scaling and distribution-analysis results remain unchanged. v2 Tables 3 and 5 disagree on the dialogue/QA MLP scores: 66.86/64.07 versus peaks of 64.07/66.86.

T1.justification: The kNN formulation, KL/CE objective, and interpolation mathematics are retained or equivalently restated. v1's FLOP-ratio derivation and scaling equations remain in v2 Appendices E–F. No substantive new theorem, proof, assumption, or derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 makes direct QA performance and an alternative to both RAG and fine-tuning central claims, highlighting 12.3% relative QA improvement and a 5.2-point general-NLP gain. v1's headline 80× kNN and 1.3× decoder speedups are replaced by 2.5× RAG and 5.6× kNN claims under different settings. The explicit StrategyQA improvement claim disappears, while scaling claims remain in the appendix.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations attributing RAG failures to contextual distractors and general-task gains to useful inductive biases from learned retrieval patterns. Its interpolation discussion adds failure behavior at extreme weights. v1's explicit limitations concerning corpus scale and one-time preprocessing overhead disappear, while the scaling and output-distribution interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a detailed training table covering warmup, epochs, batch size, gradient accumulation, and sample limits, plus specific baseline configurations; reported hardware changes from 8 to 32 A800 GPUs. However, v1's GPT2 training-step/learning-rate details and 1024-token context/512-token scoring instructions disappear despite retained scaling results. Both PDFs promise future code release, with v2 specifying release upon acceptance.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for the new QA benchmarks, BGE, efficient kNN-LM, xRAG, and DCPMI, while removing references associated with dropped evaluations and parts of the earlier motivation. Positioning against CPT and LoRA becomes more explicit, but the related-work themes and principal methodological precedents remain.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, method explanation, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Preliminary material becomes a separate section, experimental setup and results are separated, related work moves after the experiments, and scaling/FLOP analyses move to appendices. New editorial-use and reproducibility statements replace parts of the earlier appendix structure.

P2.justification: v2 adds a performance/efficiency summary, a conceptual illustration, and four case-study displays, with one example repeated in Figures 3 and 9. Main tables are substantially restructured with colored changes, and retained ablations are enlarged and reformatted. The architecture and several analyses are relocated, while the StrategyQA table and old latency panel disappear.

improvement.justification: The new QA experiments and RAG timing comparison test efficient knowledge access more directly, and the added training table improves documentation. However, v2 removes v1's five-seed reporting and some evaluation coverage and reproducibility details. Its main HaluEval table also conflicts with the appendix on scores underlying a headline claim. These substantive benefits and reporting weaknesses leave the net direction of overall quality uncertain.
